sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Pendleton County, KY?
sections.html:
Three offices in Falmouth handle the tax side of a house sale: the sheriff bills and collects, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value, and the county clerk records the deed and keeps delinquent bills. Pendleton County's government site links to the PVA's own website, so start there for parcel values and homestead forms.

  • Sheriff: 202 Chapel Street, Falmouth. The tax line is 859-654-4511.
  • County Clerk: 233 Main Street, Room 1, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 112, Falmouth, KY 41040. Call 859-654-3380. The office opens Monday to Friday from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, plus the second and last Saturday of each month from 8:30 AM to 12:00 PM, except on holiday weekends.
  • Planning and Zoning: serves the unincorporated county and the City of Falmouth with floodplain management, addressing, code enforcement and development review.

The sheriff's page states that tax bills go to the property owner only. Mortgage companies do not receive a copy, so a seller with an escrow account should still check with the lender before assuming the bill is covered.

sections.h2: What is the 2026 property tax calendar in Pendleton County?
sections.html:
Pendleton County mailed its 2026 tax statements on September 30, 2026, in a standard envelope with blue lettering that reads "2026 Pendleton County Tax Statement." An owner who has no bill by October 12 should phone the sheriff. The office takes cash, checks and credit or debit cards, with a convenience fee on cards and no American Express.

Pendleton County Sheriff collection windows for the 2026 tax year, with the amount due on a sample $1,000 bill

The sample column is simple arithmetic on the percentages the sheriff posts. The sheriff's office closes on county and state holidays and the weekends beside them, and the posted closures include Veterans Day, Thanksgiving week, Christmas week, New Year's, Martin Luther King Day and a half day on Good Friday. A secured drop box at the front door of the office takes payments, and the sheriff says it is watched by video security. Put the top portion of the bill and a phone number on the check, add a self-addressed stamped envelope if you want a paid receipt, and never leave cash in the box.

sections.h2: How does a Pendleton County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
An appeal starts with a conference with the PVA or a deputy, and only after that can the owner file with the county clerk. The Kentucky Department of Revenue says the filing deadline is the close of business on the day after the roll inspection ends.

  • Values are fixed as of January 1, and real estate is listed with the PVA from January 1 to March 1.
  • The tax roll is open to the public for 13 days starting the first Monday in May, Saturdays included.
  • The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days after inspection closes and sits for no more than five days without an extension.
  • Evidence carries the case: insurance policies, construction costs, sales listings and the physical features of the land and buildings.

If the bills print before the appeal ends, they use the number the owner claimed. A supplemental bill follows if the board lands higher. Walking away from a scheduled hearing ends the owner's path to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

sections.h2: Does the homestead exemption lower a Pendleton County bill?
sections.html:
It can, for owners who are 65 or older or classified as totally disabled. The exemption comes off the assessed value of the home, and the figure for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years is $49,100. Applications go to the PVA, and proof of age can be a birth certificate, driver's license or passport.

The Census Bureau lists $159,800 as the median value of an owner-occupied home in Pendleton County. Taking $49,100 off a house at that value leaves $110,700 to be taxed. Disability claims must be renewed each year unless the owner is a veteran with a service-connected disability or has been found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What if the Pendleton County tax is unpaid when I sell?
sections.html:
The debt stays with the parcel. Under KRS 134.015(5), the lien for delinquent tax runs up to 11 years no matter who owns the property, so a title search at closing will find it and the payoff comes out of the seller's proceeds.

After the close of business on April 15, the sheriff hands unpaid bills to the county clerk as certificates of delinquency. Interest runs at 1% a month, and the Department of Revenue adds a 10% clerk fee and a 20% county attorney fee to the total. The county attorney mails a 30-day notice and a second notice, and the clerk must hold the sale at least 90 days but not more than 135 days after the handover. The clerk's website links to the list of advertised delinquent bills. Any seller behind on taxes should ask the clerk for a written payoff figure before signing a contract.

Once a certificate is sold to a third-party purchaser, the owner deals with that purchaser, and substantial added fees apply. Settling with the clerk before the sale date avoids that step.

sections.h2: What does a seller owe the Pendleton County Clerk at closing?
sections.html:
The seller owes Kentucky's real estate transfer tax, $0.50 for each $500 of value or fraction of it, under KRS 142.050. The clerk collects it before accepting the deed. A house at the Census median of $159,800 works out to $160.00, since the value rounds up to 320 units of $500.

  • The clerk's posted fee for recording a deed is $50.00, with $3.00 more for each page after the fifth.
  • A mortgage costs $80.00 to record, and a release of mortgage costs $46.00.
  • Every deed must carry a sworn consideration statement signed by both parties and an in-care-of address for the next tax bill (KRS 382.135).
  • Exempt transfers include deeds between spouses, foreclosure transfers and deeds between parent and child for nominal consideration.

Ask the clerk's office to confirm current fees before the closing, since the posted schedule notes that amounts can shift slightly.

sections.h2: What should sellers know about Pendleton County itself?
sections.html:
Pendleton County sits in northern Kentucky, about halfway between Cincinnati and Lexington. It covers roughly 280 square miles, and its Ohio River frontage runs along the northeast edge. Falmouth, the county seat, grew at the point where the Main and South Licking rivers meet. Butler lies 10 miles north on the Licking, and DeMossville is the other named community. The county was created in 1798 and belongs to the Cincinnati metropolitan area.

Water shapes what buyers ask about. Kincaid Lake State Park offers 850 acres of camping, golf and fishing, and the county's own Planning and Zoning office runs floodplain management, so homes near the Licking deserve a flood zone check before listing. The county's public schools include Pendleton County High School north of Falmouth, Sharp Middle School, Northern Elementary in Butler and Southern Elementary in Falmouth.

The Census Bureau counts 14,800 residents as of 2025, up 1.1% from the 2020 base. About 74.7% of homes are owner-occupied, median household income runs $64,669, and and workers average 36.4 minutes of travel to their jobs.

faqs.q: When were 2026 Pendleton County property tax bills mailed?
faqs.a: They were mailed on September 30, 2026, according to the sheriff's page. A homeowner without a bill by October 12 should call the sheriff at 859-654-4511.

faqs.q: What penalty applies after January 31 in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: A 21% penalty applies from February 1 through April 15. January payments carry a 5% penalty, and the sheriff posts these windows for the 2026 bills.

faqs.q: Where does the Pendleton County Clerk record a deed?
faqs.a: At 233 Main Street, Room 1, in Falmouth. The office is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, and on the second and last Saturday of the month, 8:30 AM to noon.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a Pendleton County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it, as the grantor named in the deed. The rate is $0.50 per $500 of value, so a $159,800 sale produces $160.00.

faqs.q: Can I file a property tax appeal without talking to the PVA first?
faqs.a: No. The owner must hold a conference with the PVA or a deputy before the appeal goes to the county clerk, and the filing is due the workday after the roll inspection period ends.
